_comment: Mechanical facts about each tool — what it touches, whether it has an inverse,
and what role its arguments require. NOT a policy: there is no verdict anywhere in
this file, and no severity. The same entry yields ALLOW, HOLD, BLOCK or BLOCK_HARD
for the same tool depending on the signed plan and the arguments. Change the plan,
leave this file alone, and the verdict changes.
These are facts the person who wrote the MCP server knows and we do not get to
choose. Every reads/writes entry below was read off the SQL in mcp_servers/*.py.
Deviation from docs/v3.md §2.2, deliberately: its example gives promote_model
inverse 'registry-mcp.demote_model'. No such tool exists in this surface, so the
inverse is null. Stating an inverse we do not have would be the one kind of lie
